slot.brief: Gaseous equilibrium (e.g., PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2 or AB2 type) starting from pure reactant at given total pressure; compute α from Kp with a quadratic — full ICE algebra.

stem: Pure $\text{PCl}_5(g)$ reaches equilibrium in $\text{PCl}_5(g)\rightleftharpoons\text{PCl}_3(g)+\text{Cl}_2(g)$. At equilibrium, the total pressure is $4.0\ \text{atm}$ and $K_p=0.90\ \text{atm}$, with pressures expressed in atm. What is the degree of dissociation, $\alpha$?

verdicts.working: For initial pure PCl₅, equilibrium mole fractions are (1−α)/(1+α) for PCl₅ and α/(1+α) for each product. Thus Kₚ = 4α²/(1−α²) = 0.90 atm, giving α² = 9/49 and α = 3/7.

working:
For initial $1$ mol, equilibrium moles are $(1-\alpha,\alpha,\alpha)$; $n_{\text{tot}}=1+\alpha$. $K_p=P\dfrac{\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2}$, so $\dfrac{0.90}{4.0}=\dfrac{9}{40}=\dfrac{\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2}$. Thus $49\alpha^2=9$ and $\alpha=\dfrac{3}{7}$.

Independent check: For initial pure PCl₅, equilibrium mole fractions are (1−α)/(1+α) for PCl₅ and α/(1+α) for each product. Thus Kₚ = 4α²/(1−α²) = 0.90 atm, giving α² = 9/49 and α = 3/7.
solution:
For initial $1$ mol of $\text{PCl}_5$, equilibrium moles are $(1-\alpha,\alpha,\alpha)$, so $n_{\text{tot}}=1+\alpha$.
$$K_p=P\frac{\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2},\qquad \frac{0.90}{4.0}=\frac{9}{40}=\frac{\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2}$$
Thus $49\alpha^2=9$, giving $\alpha=\dfrac{3}{7}$.
